title: Introduction to Computing Sciences
description: The first computing course (formerly CSC 101, An Introduction to Computer Science): computer science as a discipline, the history and generations of computers, categories of computers and their hardware, software and programming languages, number systems and data representation, problem solving with algorithms, flowcharts and Python, and computer networks and the Internet. Built from the CSC 101 lecture slides (weeks 1 to 7, and the compiled slide set) and the tests and sample questions from 2016 to 2025.

topics.title: Computer Science as a Discipline
topics.summary: Computer science is the systematic study of algorithmic processes that describe and transform information. Computer scientists build models and theories, then tools, judged by six goals from correctness to intelligence.
subtopics: Definitions and the question of what can be automated
Founding traditions: mathematics, engineering and science
Six goals for computational tools and the digital divide

topics.title: History and Generations of Computers
topics.summary: Computing grew from counting aids such as the abacus through mechanical calculators to the electronic stored-program computer. The generations are named by their technology: vacuum tubes, transistors, integrated circuits, then LSI and VLSI chips.
subtopics: Early aids: abacus, Napier's bones and the slide rule
Babbage, Ada Lovelace, Boole and Hollerith
The war years: Turing, Colossus, Mark I and ENIAC
The transistor and the stored-program concept
The five generations and Moore's law

topics.title: Computer Categories and Hardware
topics.summary: Computers are special-purpose or general-purpose, and general-purpose machines range from microcomputers to supercomputers. Almost all follow the von Neumann architecture: input and output, memory, and a CPU, linked by buses.
subtopics: The von Neumann architecture and the system unit
The CPU: control unit, ALU, the machine cycle and buses
Secondary storage, input and output devices

topics.title: Software and Programming Languages
topics.summary: Software is the set of instructions that makes hardware useful, divided into system software and application software. Programming languages range from machine language through assembly language to high-level languages that need translators.
subtopics: System software: operating systems, translators, linkers and loaders

topics.title: Number Systems and Data Representation
topics.summary: Computers represent numbers, text, sound and images in binary. COS 101 covers number bases and conversions, negative and real numbers, character sets, compression and the basic logic gates.
subtopics: Positional number systems: binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal
Negative numbers, overflow and floating point

topics.title: Problem Solving: Algorithms, Flowcharts and Python
topics.summary: Problems are solved with the software development method, from specification to documentation. Algorithms are written as pseudocode or flowcharts using sequence, selection and repetition, then implemented in a language such as Python.
subtopics: Implementation in Python: variables, operators and expressions
Python if, elif and while; testing and documentation

topics.title: Computer Networks and the Internet
topics.summary: A computer network connects two or more autonomous computers to share resources and information. The Internet is a network of networks using TCP/IP, with IP addresses, domain names, URLs and services such as the Web, e-mail and FTP.
subtopics: Topologies: bus, star, tree, ring and mesh
The Internet: history, packet switching and TCP/IP
IP addresses, subnet masks, DNS and URLs
Web, e-mail, FTP, intranets, extranets and firewalls
